title: Choosing between skulle and ville
goal: Use skulle and ville to express plans, reported future, willingness, and hypothetical meaning.

objectives.statement: Use skulle and ville to express plans, reported future, willingness, and hypothetical meaning.

spans.value: Nora, Emil, and Sara are organizing a small neighbourhood market. They agreed on several jobs earlier in the week, but Saturday morning is not going exactly as planned.
Du sa at du skulle møte Sara ved samfunnshuset klokka ni.

blocks.translation: You said that you were going to meet Sara at the community centre at nine.

spans.value: Ja, vi skulle møtes klokka ni, men hun skrev at hun skulle bli forsinket.

blocks.translation: Yes, we were supposed to meet at nine, but she wrote that she would be late.

spans.value: Sa hun at hun fortsatt ville hjelpe til?

blocks.translation: Did she say that she was still willing to help?

spans.value: Ja, hun skrev at hun fortsatt ville hjelpe og gjerne lage kaffe. Hun spurte også hva vi ville gjøre hvis det begynte å regne.

blocks.translation: Yes, she wrote that she was still willing to help and would gladly make coffee. She also asked what we would do if it started to rain.

spans.value: Hvis det begynte å regne, ville vi flytte bordene inn.

blocks.translation: If it started to rain, we would move the tables inside.

spans.value: God idé. Jeg skulle egentlig hente bordene nå, men bilen min starter ikke.

blocks.translation: Good idea. I was actually supposed to collect the tables now, but my car won’t start.

spans.value: Jeg kan kjøre. Skulle du også hente skiltene?

blocks.translation: Were you also going to collect the signs?

spans.value: Ja. Hvis skiltene var lettere, ville jeg ta bussen.

blocks.translation: Yes. If the signs were lighter, I would take the bus.

spans.value: Compare these sentences carefully. In the second situation, Anna needed someone to visit and help her:

no.value: Jeg skulle besøke Anna.

en.value: I was going to visit Anna.

no.value: Jeg ville besøke Anna.

en.value: I was willing to visit Anna.

spans.value: The first sentence presents the visit as an earlier plan. In the stated help context, the second presents the speaker as willing to make the visit.
Another contrast. In the second situation, the group asked whether anyone was willing to join the trip:

no.value: Per skulle bli med på turen.

en.value: Per was going to come on the trip.

no.value: Per ville bli med på turen.

en.value: Per was willing to come on the trip.

spans.value: Plans and willingness can overlap. Context and the modal show whether the speaker emphasizes an existing arrangement or someone’s readiness to act.

sections.title: Skulle for future viewed from the past

spans.value: can express future seen from an earlier time, often called future in the past (
), when the report preserves a recoverable earlier
-type plan, schedule, expectation, promise, or commitment.
At the moment Sara wrote her message, being late was still in the future:

no.value: Sara skrev at hun skulle bli forsinket.

en.value: Sara wrote that she would be late.

no.value: Læreren sa at prøven skulle begynne klokka ti.

en.value: The teacher said that the test would begin at ten.

no.value: Jonas lovet at han skulle sende dokumentet samme kveld.

en.value: Jonas promised that he would send the document that evening.

no.value: De trodde at toget skulle gå fra spor fire.

en.value: They thought that the train would leave from platform four.

no.value: Mina fortalte at hun skulle flytte til Tromsø i august.

en.value: Mina said that she was going to move to Tromsø in August.

spans.value: The event is future relative to the earlier saying, promising, or thinking. This chapter uses
when the report preserves an earlier
meaning: a plan, schedule, expectation, promise, or commitment. Norwegian
can also have future-in-the-past readings, so past viewpoint alone does not always determine the modal.
Compare two reports with explicit source contexts. First, Maja had announced:

no.value: Maja sa at hun skulle bli med.

en.value: Maja said that she would come along.

spans.value: Later, when the group asked who was willing to join, Maja volunteered:

no.value: Maja sa at hun ville bli med.

en.value: Maja said that she was willing to come along.

spans.value: The first preserves an earlier plan expressed with
. The second uses the stated request-and-volunteer context to emphasize past willingness. Without such context, an isolated clause with
can also receive a future-in-the-past reading.

no.value: Han sa at han skulle komme senere.

en.value: He said that he would come later.

spans.value: can also express future in the past in other contexts. Choose from the source meaning and surrounding context, not from the English word alone.
. In a past narrative or report, it can show that someone was willing or ready to act. A request, need, or voluntary offer in the context establishes that meaning.
When the market group needed someone to prepare drinks:

no.value: Sara ville lage kaffe.

en.value: Sara was willing to make coffee.

no.value: Ingen andre hadde tid, men Amir ville hjelpe.

en.value: Nobody else had time, but Amir was willing to help.

spans.value: When the family needed a driver:

no.value: Bestefar ville gjerne kjøre oss til stasjonen.

en.value: Grandfather was happy to drive us to the station.

spans.value: can make an expression sound positive, but it does not by itself distinguish willingness from desire. Outside this chapter’s scored distinction, context can give

no.value: Barna ville se filmen en gang til.

en.value: The children wanted to watch the film again.

no.value: Jeg ville gjerne snakke med deg.

en.value: I wanted to speak with you.

no.value: Hun sa at hun gjerne ville delta.

en.value: She said that she would like to participate.

spans.value: The negative form can express refusal or lack of willingness:

no.value: Katten ville ikke gå ut.

en.value: The cat would not go outside.

no.value: Han ville ikke svare på spørsmålet.

en.value: He would not answer the question.

spans.value: may mean did not want to or refused to.

no.value: Nora skulle kjøre Emil.

en.value: Nora was going to drive Emil.

spans.value: When Emil needed a driver, Nora said that she was ready to help:

no.value: Nora ville kjøre Emil.

en.value: Nora was willing to drive Emil.

spans.value: The first is about the arrangement. In the stated past context, the second is about Nora’s willingness.

no.value: De skulle hjelpe oss på lørdag.

en.value: They were going to help us on Saturday.

no.value: De ville hjelpe oss på lørdag.

en.value: They were willing to help us on Saturday.

spans.value: merely because a person had an intention. If the main point is an agreed schedule or arrangement,
for what would happen in an imagined situation. A common pattern combines a hypothetical condition (

no.value: Hvis det regnet, ville vi flytte bordene inn.

en.value: If it rained, we would move the tables inside.

no.value: Hvis jeg hadde mer tid, ville jeg lære samisk.

en.value: If I had more time, I would learn Sami.

no.value: Hvis leiligheten var billigere, ville vi leie den.

en.value: If the flat were cheaper, we would rent it.

no.value: Hvis hun bodde nærmere, ville vi besøke henne oftere.

en.value: If she lived closer, we would visit her more often.

spans.value: The past-tense form in the condition does not necessarily describe past time. It helps present the situation as imagined, uncertain, or contrary to present reality.
The condition can also come second:

no.value: Jeg ville gå mer på ski hvis jeg bodde nærmere fjellet.

en.value: I would ski more if I lived closer to the mountains.

no.value: Vi ville kjøpe huset hvis det hadde et større kjøkken.

en.value: We would buy the house if it had a larger kitchen.

spans.value: Sometimes the condition is understood from context rather than stated:

no.value: Med bedre vær ville flere mennesker komme.

en.value: With better weather, more people would come.

no.value: Uten bilen ville turen ta mye lengre tid.

en.value: Without the car, the journey would take much longer.

spans.value: Questions follow the same meaning pattern:

no.value: Hva ville du gjøre hvis du fant en lommebok på gata?

en.value: What would you do if you found a wallet in the street?

no.value: Hvor ville dere bo hvis dere kunne velge fritt?

en.value: Where would you live if you could choose freely?

spans.value: in both examples, but Norwegian makes the meaning distinction visible:

no.value: Hun sa at hun skulle kjøpe huset.

en.value: She said that she would buy the house.

no.value: Hun ville kjøpe huset hvis det var billigere.

en.value: She would buy the house if it were cheaper.

spans.value: In the first sentence, the report preserves her earlier stated plan to buy the house. In the second, buying it depends on an imagined condition.

no.value: De trodde at mange mennesker skulle komme.

en.value: They thought that many people would come.

no.value: Med bedre vær ville mange mennesker komme.

en.value: With better weather, many people would come.

Mistake 3: Adding å after the modal

sections.title: Cumulative transfer: a delayed cabin trip

spans.value: Imagine that four friends planned a weekend at a cabin. Some arrangements changed, different people offered help, and bad weather made the group consider alternatives.

prompt.value: Revisit the market preparation examples. Choose the complete interpretation that identifies what each use of skulle points back to and whether completion is asserted.

options.text: All three statements present willingness to act: Emil was willing to collect the tables, the group was willing to eat, and the bus was willing to arrive.
options.why: The contexts describe arrangements or expectations, not people’s willingness.

options.text: All three statements describe imagined results that depend on an unstated condition.
options.why: Imagined results are taught with ville; these statements refer to earlier plans or expectations.

options.text: Emil’s job was previously arranged, the meal was an earlier arrangement, and the bus arrival was an earlier expectation or schedule. None of the three statements guarantees that the action happened.
options.why: Skulle presents a recoverable earlier plan, arrangement, or expectation, not the final result.

options.text: All three statements say that the actions definitely happened as planned.
options.why: The lesson states that skulle describes the plan or expectation, whether or not the action was completed.

stem.value: Read these statements: 1. Emil skulle hente bordene. — Emil was going to collect the tables. 2. Vi skulle spise sammen på fredag. — We were supposed to eat together on Friday. 3. Bussen skulle komme klokka halv ti. — The bus was due to arrive at half past nine.

prompt.value: Fill every blank. Use the form and infinitive that express an earlier plan or expectation rather than personal willingness.

spans.value: For an appointment arranged earlier: Jeg
For a household job arranged earlier: Emil
For an earlier shared arrangement: Vi

prompt.value: Write four short Norwegian past reports, one for each earlier statement below. Preserve the explicit earlier skal-type plan, schedule, promise, or announcement with skulle + infinitive. 1. Emil earlier said: Jeg skal hente bordene. Report this later. 2. The timetable earlier stated: Bussen skal komme klokka halv ti. Report this later. 3. Jonas earlier promised: Jeg skal sende dokumentet samme kveld. Report the promise later. 4. The teacher earlier announced: Prøven skal begynne klokka ti. Report the announcement later.

payload.judge_prompt: Check all four Norwegian reports against the task and report evidence for each criterion. Accept natural variations in reporting verb, subject reference, and word order when the earlier plan, schedule, promise, or announcement remains clear. Require skulle followed by an infinitive for these explicit earlier skal contexts. If a supplied report genuinely leaves skulle and future-in-the- past ville equally natural, accept either modal when the surrounding wording supports that reading.

The first sentence must frame an earlier arrangement with skulle + infinitive; the second must frame contextually established willingness with ville + infinitive after a stated need or request.

Presents Nora’s readiness to act in response to Emil’s need using *ville* + infinitive.
States in Norwegian that *skulle* marks the arrangement while *ville* marks contextual past willingness.

Require skulle + infinitive in the two reports of explicit earlier skal statements, and ville + infinitive in the two imagined results with conditional meaning. Accept natural variations in subjects and reporting verbs. If a report genuinely leaves both modals natural, accept either only when the learner’s wording supports that reading.

criteria.instruction: Selects *skulle* for both reports that preserve explicit earlier *skal* meanings.
Selects *ville* + infinitive for both results that depend on imagined conditions.
Keeps reported earlier plans or promises distinct from hypothetical results across all four sentences.

prompt.value: Choose the complete interpretation of every modal occurrence in this continuation of the market scene.

options.text: 1. skulle komme senere reports willingness. 2. ville kjøre meg reports an earlier arrangement. 3. ville lage kaffe is a hypothetical result. 4. ville jeg lage kaffe reports willingness. 5. skulle stå på kjøkkenet expresses willingness. 6. skulle ta den med is a hypothetical result.
options.why: The dialogue explicitly marks 2 and 3 as willingness, but 1, 4, 5, and 6 have different meanings.

options.text: 1. skulle komme senere reports an expected event and preserves an earlier skal-type meaning. 2. ville kjøre meg expresses the neighbour’s willingness. 3. ville lage kaffe reports Sara’s earlier willingness. 4. ville jeg lage kaffe is a hypothetical result dependent on finding a thermos. 5. skulle stå på kjøkkenet expresses an expectation about the thermos’s location. 6. skulle ta den med reports Jakob’s earlier plan or commitment.
options.why: The connected context distinguishes reported expectation or commitment, willingness, and hypothetical result.

options.text: All six occurrences report earlier plans or expectations, including the two occurrences of ville.
options.why: The conditional result in 4 and the willingness readings in 2 and 3 are not earlier arrangements.

options.text: All six occurrences describe imagined results, because every English translation contains a form of would.
options.why: English would does not determine one Norwegian modal; only 4 has hypothetical result meaning here.

stem.value: Read the dialogue: 1. Vi trodde at du skulle komme senere. — We thought that you would come later. 2. Det trodde jeg også, men naboen min ville kjøre meg. — I thought so too, but my neighbour was willing to drive me. 3. Flott! Du sa tidligere at du ville lage kaffe. Har du fortsatt lyst til det? — Great! You said earlier that you were willing to make coffee. Do you still want to? 4. Ja. Hvis dere fant en stor termos, ville jeg lage kaffe til alle. — Yes. If you found a large thermos, I would make coffee for everyone. 5. Termosen skulle stå på kjøkkenet, men jeg finner den ikke. — The thermos was supposed to be in the kitchen, but I cannot find it. 6. Jakob sa at han skulle ta den med. Jeg ringer ham. — Jakob said that he would bring it. I will call him.

prompt.value: Write a short connected Norwegian account of a delayed cabin trip, followed by a short follow-up message. Use the new cabin situation and include all four meanings in the connected text: - one earlier arrangement for the trip, expressed with skulle + infinitive; - one later report preserving a friend’s explicit earlier skal-type plan or commitment, expressed with skulle + infinitive; - one earlier response to a stated request or need for help, expressed with ville + infinitive; - one imagined bad-weather result that depends on a condition, expressed with ville + infinitive. Make the account and follow-up message show why each modal is chosen.

payload.judge_prompt: Check the connected cabin account and follow-up message against every criterion. Accept natural cabin vocabulary, infinitives, subjects, and sentence order when each required meaning is clear. Accept either modal for a reported context only when the learner’s supplied wording genuinely leaves skulle and future-in-the-past ville equally natural. Do not require copied lesson sentences.
